newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to move narrowly despite yen's fall.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to move narrowly despite yen's fall.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are seen likely to hover in a narrow range on Monday. The yen's sharp decline against the dollar following Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting will inspire buying of blue-chip exporters' shares, but a recent rally will make participants cautious, brokers said.
On Friday, the key 225-share Nikkei average closed down 85.21 points or 0.46 percent at 18,612.86. Its June futures fell 70 points to 18,630.
The dollar jumped close to 127 yen in early Asian trade on Monday after the G7 failed to specifically mention "yen weakness" as a shared concern, currency traders said.

"The weaker yen will encourage buying of blue chips, but any rise would be limited, as the TOPIX index (of all first section stocks) has already rallied for seven days in a row," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
"The Nikkei 225 is likely to take a rest for a week or so and then will head higher again," he said.

Aside from the effects on the currency markets, the G7 meeting did not yield anything that could affect the stock market, brokers said. "There was nothing particular in the G7 communique," one trader at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
The dollar jumped above 127 yen in early Asian trade on Monday after the G7 failed to specifically mention yen weakness as a shared concern. The U.S. currency was quoted at 126.80 yen at 0102 GMT.
